capabilities: Render ```wireloom code blocks as self-contained SVG wireframes
Adapt wireframe rendering to light and dark Obsidian themes
Draw leader-line annotations along SVG edges
Report syntax errors with line, column and correction hints
Configure render theme and maximum display width
disambiguation: Not a diagramming tool for flowcharts or graphs; it only renders the Wireloom wireframe language as UI mockups.
extras: Pending Obsidian community plugin review; manual install currently requires building with Node.js/npm (BRAT also supported). Requires Obsidian v0.15.0+. Community-driven and not an official Wireloom product. Known limits: rendered wireframes do not auto-refresh on theme change, and the bundled Wireloom JS library may lag behind the protocol.
motivation: The author built it so that LLM-generated interface prototypes can live directly in documents as text, enabling product managers, developers and designers to embed and iterate wireframes without tool switching.
problem: Obsidian has no way to render text-based UI wireframe specs inside notes, so embedding interface prototypes means pasting screenshots or maintaining external files.

relations.evidence: seamlessly integrates Wireloom — a text-based wireframe language designed for AI agents — into Obsidian's Markdown rendering pipeline

summary: Renders ```wireloom fenced code blocks as self-contained SVG UI wireframes inside notes, aimed at AI-generated interface prototypes.
